subtopics.title: The Mole-Ratio Method at Grade 11 Speed

questions.question: The only quantity permitted to cross a balanced equation is:
For 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃, the maximum mass of aluminium oxide from 10,8 g of aluminium (excess oxygen) is:
Crossing from aluminium to aluminium oxide in 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃, the correct ratio fraction is:
options: Two over four — wanted over given

questions.question: The theoretical yield of a reaction is:
options: The mass actually collected in the laboratory
The average of several experimental results
The yield after impurities are removed
The maximum product the balanced equation allows from the given reactants

subtopics.title: The Limiting Reagent — Who Runs Out First

questions.question: The limiting reagent of a reaction is the reactant that:
options: Has the smallest number of moles
Is used up first, stopping the reaction

questions.question: For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, 14 g of nitrogen (0,5 mol) is mixed with 2,4 g of hydrogen (1,2 mol). The limiting reagent is:
options: Nitrogen, because 0,5 mol is the smaller amount
Hydrogen, because 0,5 mol of nitrogen demands 1,5 mol of hydrogen and only 1,2 mol is available
Nitrogen, because its molar mass is larger
Neither — the mixture is in perfect ratio

questions.question: In that reaction, the mass of nitrogen left over when the reaction stops is:
Every product calculation must be built on:
options: The reactant with the smaller molar mass
The total mass of both reactants

questions.question: Percentage yield is calculated as:
options: Actual yield ÷ mass of limiting reagent × 100
Mass of pure substance ÷ mass of sample × 100

questions.question: A reaction's theoretical yield is 20,4 g and 17,34 g is collected. The percentage yield is:
A 20 g rock sample with excess H₂SO₄ releases 4,48 dm³ of CO₂ at STP (0,2 mol). The percentage purity of MgCO₃ (M = 84 g·mol⁻¹) is:
A calculated percentage yield of 112 % most likely indicates:
options: Wet or contaminated product, or unreacted material weighed with the goods
A catalyst that created extra product
A mistake in the balanced equation

subtopics.title: Airbags and Explosions — Stoichiometry at Speed

questions.question: The airbag decomposition of sodium azide is:
97,5 g of NaN₃ (M = 65 g·mol⁻¹) decomposes completely. The volume of nitrogen at STP is:
To a chemist, an explosion is defined by:
options: A loud noise and a flame
The very rapid production of a large gas volume from a small volume of solid or liquid
A reaction that requires a spark

subtopics.title: The Ingredient That Runs Out First

questions.question: Lemonade needs 4 lemons + 1 cup of sugar per jug. With 20 lemons and 6 cups of sugar, the stand can make:
options: 5 jugs, with 1 cup of sugar left over

questions.question: The lemons limit the stand even though sugar is the smaller number because:
options: The recipe consumes lemons four times as fast — only the ratio test decides
Lemons always run out before sugar
Sugar dissolves and cannot run out
The smaller number is always in excess

questions.question: The chemistry version of the ratio test begins by:
options: Choosing the reactant with the largest coefficient

subtopics.title: What the Kitchen Promised and What Reached the Plate

questions.question: The recipe promised 5 jugs; 4 reached the customers. The percentage yield is:
Which is NOT a genuine reason for a yield below 100 %?
options: Product lost during transfers between containers
Atoms being destroyed in the reaction

questions.question: Six jugs from a five-jug recipe mirrors a laboratory yield over 100 %, which means:
options: The reaction beat its theoretical ceiling
Something extra was counted — wet or contaminated product

questions.question: In a purity determination, the acid is supplied in excess so that:
options: Every scrap of the genuine substance reacts, while the impurities react with nothing
The gas is produced more slowly
The acid becomes the limiting reagent

subtopics.title: The Pillow That Inflates Before You Blink

questions.question: An airbag fills because a small solid pellet:
options: Decomposes into a huge volume of nitrogen gas within milliseconds
Sucks in air from the cabin

questions.question: 97,5 g of azide is 1,5 mole-crates; the recipe pays 3 crates of gas per 2 crates of azide; each gas crate fills 22,4 dm³. The bag volume is:
Engineers determine the pellet mass by:
options: Testing pellets of every size in crashes
Choosing the heaviest pellet that fits the wheel
Running the stoichiometry backwards from the bag volume to grams of azide
Matching the pellet to the car's mass

questions.question: A quarry charge and an airbag share the same core chemistry, namely:
options: Both consume oxygen from the air
Violent, rapid gas production from a small solid — the airbag simply catches the gas in a bag
